mathematics: Actual empirical key cardinal is k times finite bin count times the imported exact profile count. Fixed bin and pile factors are absorbed with the remaining epsilon/2 power.
Expectation of rows in a fixed full-word set equals |R| times its exact product mass, by fixed-count cylinder marginals and finite Fubini; no row independence is used.
Actual boundary and extension exception sets inject into full-word rare positions. Both boundary truncations are controlled by the same rare-count event, and the extension by a second event.
Source rare-tail estimates give expected discarded rows at most N^(-D), with C chosen before chi. Actual unique boundary/stable partition gives retained-or-discarded coverage.

Every actual retained block has a valid finite descriptor. Its good-cost bin bound follows from the original-N logarithmic horizon; the number of realized classes is bounded by the descriptor universe.
public_type_and_model: N is the original scale throughout, even when current n is smaller. Discard theorem includes 0<n<=N; class count does not need n<=N and therefore proves a stronger uniform statement.
Discard threshold chi0 is independent of N,n,d,cuts,R,delta after fixing k,T,D,C. Count threshold N0 follows chi and width and precedes all arrays and anchor sets.
RetainedBlock is the literal three source truncations on actual valid boundary/stable blocks, rather than a supplied partition certificate.
adversarial: Terminal boundary at the last future column yields a full singleton word, including genuine crossing there.
Zero columns and zero-probability digits are handled by Legal/full-cylinder premises and exact expectation identities; current n=0 is excluded where its profile is used.
Strict exceedance of floor budgets is converted to integer budget+1; no loss of one in the rare-event bound.
Descriptor collisions reduce image cardinal and do not affect the upper bound; a class-fiber entropy proof is still separately necessary.
remaining: Actual class-fiber entropy and scalar exponent substitutions, physical graph assembly and concrete F.
